subject: trap-jaw ant
title: This Ant's Jaws Snap 2,300 Times Faster Than a Blink

scenes.text: This ant bites so fast that it can launch itself into the air.
The trap-jaw ant. Its jaws slam shut at up to 145 miles an hour.
Scientists needed cameras at 250,000 frames a second just to see it. A blink is 2,300 times slower.
The jaws accelerate at 100,000 times gravity, and each bite carries hundreds of times the ant's own weight.
So when a spider attacks, the ant points its jaws at the ground and bites the floor.
The bite throws it up to three inches into the air. The fastest bite in nature is also its escape button.

description:
Trap-jaw ants snap their jaws shut at up to 145 miles an hour, about 2,300 times faster than a blink.
High-speed cameras at 250,000 frames a second showed that the ant can bite the ground to launch itself away from predators like spiders.
Could you survive a day as an ant? Tell us below.
first_comment: The jaws only need about 0.13 milliseconds to close. Would you rather meet this ant or a mantis shrimp?
